Name: Taum's Inventory Hotkeys
Author: glover3175
Description:
[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]Hello, Star-dewers and Star-donters!

I love playing modded Stardew Valley on my Steam Deck or with a controller.  I have solved a very specific problem that's been plaguing my gameplay.[/color]

[color=#D4D4D8]Modded Stardew Valley, quickly accumulates a number of shortcuts. Trying to fit all of those onto a controller, or into your noggin memory is a nightmare.

The Steam Deck is fantastic. You get four additional back buttons, one problem... [i]There are only four of them[/i].[/color]

[color=#D4D4D8][b]Main features[/b][/color]
[spoiler][color=#D4D4D8]• Up to 40 hotkeys per profile, with no fixed six-profile limit.
• Profiles: create, select, and delete profiles through the mod settings.
• Quick profile switching: use inventory arrows or scroll wheel hovering over the Create hotkey icon.
• Two layouts: regular inventory tabs or a centered chest-style grid.
• Drag-and-drop reordering in chest-style view, with a setting to enable or disable it.
• Custom names, descriptions, and icons using Stardew Valley’s emoji icons.
• Controller navigation through the hotkeys, editor, and mod settings.
• Rebindable controls for keyboard/mouse and controller.
• Configurable appearance: grid dimensions, chest-grid position, profile-button placement, and optional background blur.
• Show/hide controls, plus a global hide setting.
• Tooltips showing your configured controls, including native Xbox controller glyphs.
• Sound effects and notifications for hotkey actions.
• Optional debug logging to help investigate problems.[/color][/spoiler]
Example compatible mods:
[spoiler]- Better Crafting
- Chests Anywhere
- Deluxe Journal
- Perfection Handbook
- UI Info Suite 2
- World Navigator[/spoiler]
[line]
[b][size=4]Installation instructions[/size][/b]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Install SMAPI 4.5.2 or later.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#d4d4d8]Install GMCM as a prerequisite dependency[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Extract the downloaded archive into your Stardew Valley Mods folder.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/color][/*]
[/list][line]
[b]Profiles and layouts[/b]
[spoiler]Profiles let you keep separate collections of shortcuts—for example, time controls, farming utilities, and navigation tools.

Each profile supports up to 40 hotkeys and stores its own grid dimensions. Profile files are saved under:

Mods/taums-inventory-hotkeys/profiles/hotkeys-profile-N.json

The grid supports 2–10 columns and 1–4 rows. Reducing those values changes how many hotkeys are displayed; it does not delete saved entries. Increase the grid dimensions again to display entries outside the smaller layout.
Chest-style view adjusts its displayed dimensions to the hotkeys it contains, within your configured grid limits. You can also adjust its horizontal and vertical position.

Included template profiles and keybind conflicts

Template profiles are included for some mods I use personally. They are starting points—you must configure their keybinds to match your own setup.

The templates do not change other mods’ settings or resolve conflicts automatically.

If a hotkey opens an unexpected menu or triggers several actions, check which mods use that key. Changing a hotkey here does not change the corresponding binding in another mod.

I can investigate problems with Inventory Hotkeys, but I cannot configure or troubleshoot every player’s individual collection of conflicting bindings.[/spoiler]
[line]
[b]Troubleshooting[/b]
[spoiler]If an action does nothing, first test the same shortcut directly during normal gameplay.

Check that the target mod is installed, its binding matches, and any required feature has been unlocked.

A “Hotkey triggered” notification means the configured input was sent; it cannot confirm that another mod completed the action.

If the inventory buttons themselves are unresponsive, check your configured controls and hover over or highlight the relevant component.

Enable Debug logs in the mod settings when reporting an issue, and include your SMAPI log, input device, layout, and steps to reproduce it.[/spoiler]
[line]
Current bugs / TODO's:
[spoiler]Why does it rely on [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/10505]GMCM[/url]? - I hooked into their existing keybind assigner to not fail rebuilding it in 12 hours, plus you likely are already using it to configure initial keybinds.

Why do I need a keyboard to set them up? - Because I didn't think that far ahead, I will figure out an onscreen keyboard solution (or something even better long term) if you don't want to keep rebinding keys or use a keyboard on initial setup.

Why doesn't it work with <x> mod ? I likely didn't test it, so leave it under posts and I will take a look.

Does it reflect custom themes? - I don't know, untested.

Record timed macros and playback or modify execution delay ? - Maybe at some point.
[/spoiler]
[line]
Compatability
- Works with bigger backpack
- Doesnt work with Lookup anything
- if having issues try to ensure the stardew settings UI scale and zoom match - eg 100% - 100% or 75% 75%
[line]

[color=#D4D4D8]GMCM for the controller keybinds already configured[/color]

[color=#D4D4D8]A note from the developer[/color]
[spoiler][color=#D4D4D8]After a rather long hiatus from the modding community (all the way back to Starbound Alpha ~2013, which actually kickstarted my programming career), I'm back with my first official Stardew Valley mod!

This started as a small challange to myself, a mod in less than 12 hours, to make my own heavily modded Steam Deck playthrough more enjoyable. I figured other controller players might find it useful too.

I'm a full-time developer, so while I'm absolutely open to suggestions, bug reports, and improvements, please bear with me if updates take a little time.

I hope this makes your next modded Stardew Valley playthrough a little better.[/color][/spoiler]
